properties.project_name: Pier 70 Building 113/114/115/116 (Union Iron Works Machine Shop)
properties.digitized_from: DataSF Building Footprints dataset (real, surveyed building outlines; not tied to an Assessor parcel).
properties.digitization_method: SPLIT 2026-09-16 from the combined blklot 4111004 row (previously one polygon covering Buildings 113/114 and 115/116 together, since the real Assessor lot has no further official subdivision). CORRECTED same day: an earlier version of this split attempted to separate '113/114' (3 footprint pieces) from '115/116' (1 more southerly footprint) using area matching alone. A geometry-quality check then found that southerly '115/116' footprint overlapping Pier 70 Parcel C1 (a planned, not-yet-built 90ft residential block) by 2580 sq m. Re-checked against Pier 70 D4D Figure 6.4.2 itself (page171.png in this project's cached source PDF, not the previously mis-cached 'heightplan-247.png' which turned out to be a Potrero Power Station figure): Figure 6.4.2 draws ONE undifferentiated light-gray outline box labeled '113-116' entirely NORTH of '21ST ST (NEW)' (a planned/not-yet-built street), at the same latitude band as Parcel PKN -- it does not distinguish 113/114 from 115/116 as separate shapes at all. Transforming that box's pixel bounds (pixel (643,376)-(1073,724) on page171.png) via this site's validated 6-point affine transform gives real-world bounds of lon -122.3866 to -122.3851, lat 37.7597 to 37.7608. Checking all 8 real footprints tagged mblr=SF4111004 against that box: 4 of them (~6787, ~2273, ~632, and ~59 sq m) fall inside it; the remaining 4 (the previously-misassigned ~3937 sq m piece plus 3 much smaller slivers) sit outside it, to the south, overlapping Parcel C1's footprint instead -- i.e. on land that Figure 6.4.2 treats as a separate, not-yet-built development block, not as part of the historic 113-116 complex. Since the diagram itself does not separate 113/114 from 115/116, and the previous area-based attempt to do so conflicted with the diagram's own drawn position, this feature now combines all 4 in-box footprint pieces into one 'Building 113/114/115/116' MultiPolygon rather than fabricate an unsupported split. This is REAL surveyed building geometry, not a diagram trace. CORRECTED 2026-09-17 (user-flagged: 'should expand south, currently looks like it leaves out part of the building'): the 4 pieces excluded above were dropped specifically because they fell outside Figure 6.4.2's own drawn '113-116' box and instead overlapped Parcel C1's THEN-committed position -- but that C1 position was independently found the same day to be badly mispositioned (overlapping the real, official 21st St by over 100m of its length) and has since been ground-truthed to its correct location, well clear of these pieces. Re-examined the largest excluded piece (mblr SF4111004, ~3935 sq m) directly against satellite imagery: it is visibly the same continuous roof structure as the 3 already-included northern pieces (matching roofline, skylight pattern, no gap or seam) -- unambiguously the building's own southernmost bay, not a separate structure. Re-included all 8 real footprint pieces tagged SF4111004 into this feature (previously only 4 were used); combined area increased from ~9,751 to ~13,927 sq m. This is a case where the diagram's own simplified box undersold the real building's true extent -- the real, surveyed footprint takes priority, consistent with how this project treats real building data everywhere else. Confirmed against the now-corrected C1: still overlaps it by ~1,886 sq m (about half of the re-added piece), which is expected, not an error -- this project already documents that several of Pier 70's D4D blocks are sited on existing buildings slated for demolition, and this specific real building's own historic-preservation sourcing (see regulatory_context) notes 'demolition of later metal additions on the west and south facades,' consistent with this real building's southernmost bay being at least partly removed to make way for C1. REVERSED/REFINED 2026-09-17, SAME DAY (user-flagged: 'should remain north of 21st street and not overlap with C1'): the 'expected overlap' reasoning above was a rationalization, not a validated fact -- no source actually ties the demolished additions to this specific footprint piece or to C1's specific footprint, and Figure 6.4.2 draws 113-116 entirely north of 21st St with no overlap onto any south-of-the-street parcel. Checked precisely where the real 21st St centerline (CNN 15233000/15232000) falls relative to the re-added piece: it straddles the piece -- part of the piece's own real footprint sits north of the street (legitimately part of the historic complex as mapped here) and part sits south of it (in the same space as C1). Since this project maps the D4D's planned future, not a survey of exactly what stands today, split this piece at the real 21st St curb line (6.8m north of centerline, this project's standard curb offset) and kept only the northern portion, discarding ~2,996 sq m south of the street. Confirmed 0 overlap with C1 (13.6m gap now, matching the real street's own width). Removed the EXPECTED_OVERLAP_PAIRS entry for 'Building 113-116 x Parcel C1' in check_geometry_quality.py since there is no longer a legitimate overlap to exempt.
properties.accuracy_caveat: Real, surveyed building footprints -- high confidence in each piece's outline and in the group's overall position (confirmed to sit within Figure 6.4.2's own '113-116' box). Individual identification of which piece(s) correspond to Building 113 vs 114 vs 115 vs 116 specifically is NOT possible from the sources checked -- Figure 6.4.2 draws them as one undifferentiated box, and the 2013 HPC packet's textual description ('115 and 116 abut Building 113/114') does not give a precise position. Rather than guess, this feature represents the combined complex, consistent with how it is actually shown in the source diagram. The combined footprint here (~9751 sq m / ~104,957 sqft) is larger than Building 113/114 alone (~86,100 sqft per its documented 492ft x 175ft footprint) and smaller than 113/114 + 115/116's combined documented GSF (~95,000 + ~38,000 = ~133,000 GSF) -- broadly consistent given GSF can include multi-level floor area not captured by a footprint, but not independently verified piece-by-piece.
properties.why_no_real_parcel: This parcel (blklot 4111004) has no street address in DataSF's Assessor roll. The real Assessor lot groups Buildings 113/114 and 115/116 into one polygon with no further official subdivision -- this feature uses the real building footprints instead, matched to the specific area of the lot that Figure 6.4.2 itself draws as the historic '113-116' complex.
properties.regulatory_context: Union Iron Works Machine Shop and Foundry, Buildings 113/114, on the south side of 20th Street just east of Illinois Street -- 'one of the most valuable and most vulnerable historic resources on the site' per the 2013 HPC packet (2013.1168E). Two unreinforced brick structures (Machine Shop, built 1885, and Foundry, built 1886) joined in 1914 by a reinforced concrete connector; building-length skylights, rows of high arched windows; ~95,000 GSF, 492ft long by 175ft wide, ~62ft tall. Buildings 115 and 116 abut Building 113/114, constructed 1916-1917, ~38,000 GSF, 57ft tall, with 'unusual windows and monitor skylights.' At review time the complex was red-tagged and subject to an engineer's advisory of imminent collapse. Rehab by Orton Development Inc. (ODI) included demolition/relocation of later metal additions on the west and south facades, a new steel seismic system tied into the brick perimeter, and demolition of two minor eastern appendages (Buildings 23/24, ~1,500 GSF). Proposed for industrial/warehouse/maker-space use (food, tech, life science, biotech, education, arts production) with ancillary office, showroom, and retail, alongside Building 14, framing a shared ~45,000 sf courtyard.
properties.notes: Split 2026-09-16 from the combined 'Union Iron Works Machine Shop & Foundry' entry; CORRECTED same day to merge back a mistaken 113/114-vs-115/116 sub-split once it was found to conflict with Figure 6.4.2's own undifferentiated box -- see digitization_method.
